Application Areas: Adversarial Security of Audio and IoT Systems
Privacy Preservation in Wireless Localization and Sensing
Key Research Thinking Patterns: Perception-Aware Adversarial Optimization: Integrating human perceptual models into neural network architectures to generate stealthy adversarial examples that bypass automated detection while maintaining human imperceptibility, as demonstrated by the CEMF-PA attack on YouTube's copyright system using Siamese Neural Networks.

Proactive Defensive Deception: Manipulating physical-layer signal characteristics, such as Channel State Information (CSI), to create 'ambush locations' that feed false physiological or occupancy data to eavesdroppers, effectively neutralizing inference attacks on breathing rates and crowd counts using Software-Defined Radio platforms.

Black-Box Algorithm Reverse Engineering: Exploiting side-channel data from proprietary geolocation services, specifically the Location Lookup Table (LLT) from Google's API, to reconstruct black-box localization algorithms and enable precise location spoofing without physical jamming.

Input-Agnostic Physical Layer Injection: Developing energy-minimized signal injection strategies to override RFID tag identification thresholds without prior knowledge of tag content, leveraging statistical modeling to evade detection while achieving high success rates in altering reader decoding outcomes.
Summary Description: Shangqing Zhao is a researcher specializing in the security and privacy of wireless communication systems, audio processing, and emerging quantum machine learning frameworks. Their work focuses on identifying and mitigating vulnerabilities in physical-layer protocols, including Wi-Fi geolocation, RFID authentication, and CSI-based sensing. Key contributions include the development of perception-aware adversarial attacks against audio copyright systems, proactive defensive deception mechanisms to protect user privacy from wireless inference, and novel injection attacks on RFID infrastructure. Additionally, Zhao evaluates the security implications of Quantum Machine Learning algorithms against classical counterparts, highlighting vulnerabilities to noise and adversarial perturbations. The research leverages platforms such as Software-Defined Radio, IBM Qiskit, and commercial APIs to validate theoretical models against real-world constraints.
